title: Cedar Lane Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Onboarding kickoff for Cedar Lane Health. Reviewed onboarding plan, SSO/SAML requirements, private deployment options (VPC), data retention and audit requirements. Agreed on a 4-week pilot to validate inference latency and cost, initial POC dataset and benchmark plan. Action items assigned for SSO docs, infra checklist, and security questionnaire.
next_steps: Redwood to send onboarding playbook and SSO setup doc (by 2027-08-27)
Customer to provide sample PII-free dataset and account list for pilot (by 2027-08-30)
Schedule deep-dive on VPC networking with Cedar Lane infra (week of 2027-08-30)
SE to run initial baseline benchmarks once sample data is received
action_items: Maya Patel: Send onboarding playbook and SSO/SAML setup guide - due 2027-08-27
Jordan Lee: Draft pilot benchmark plan and required sample schema - due 2027-08-30
Sara Lin (Cedar Lane): Complete security questionnaire and return to Redwood - due 2027-08-26
Marcus Reed: Share VPC network contacts and approved CIDR ranges - due 2027-08-25
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-08-23
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Redwood SE), Dan (Redwood Impl), Dr. Alicia (CTO), Marcus (Head of Platform), Sara (Security), Tom (Data Eng)

Summary: Quick intro, review onboarding timeline, SSO and private deployment questions, security/retention constraints, agree pilot scope and next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the CSM working with Cedar Lane, really excited to kick off the onboarding, we've got Jordan and Dan from our implementation team here as well.
[00:12] Dr. Alicia: Hi all, thanks, appreciate you setting this up. We'll just go through our goals and constraints on our side.
[00:18] Marcus: Quick intro, Marcus Reed, I run platform at Cedar Lane. Main objectives are: get inference into our patient triage pipeline with predictable latency, and make sure data doesn't leave our VPC.
[00:30] Sara: Hi, Sara Lin, security lead. I'll be sniffing through docs, looking for SOC2, audit logs, KMS integration, and SSO.
[00:40] Jordan: Great, perfect. I'll start with a high-level onboarding plan then dive into the technical bits.
[00:46] Jordan: Plan is usually a 4-week pilot: week 0 - SSO + infra prep, week 1 - baseline benchmarks and small scale pilot, week 2 - iterate on prompts and quantization profiles, week 3 - ramp and run regression checks, then handoff. We can adjust.
[01:10] Tom: When you say infra prep, do you mean Redwood-managed or our own VPC install? We need private deployment because PHI is involved.
[01:18] Dan: Good question. We support both Dedicated (Redwood-hosted reserved capacity) and Private (VPC / on-prem). For PHI we'd generally recommend Private with customer-managed VPC + private control plane or on-prem if you need air-gap.
[01:36] Marcus: We prefer customer-managed VPC. Can you confirm data never leaves our region? Also how does KMS work with key rotation?
[01:44] Jordan: Yes, with Private deployment we can keep inference within your VPC and region. For KMS: Redwood integrates with customer KMS/HSM for envelope encryption; key rotation is controlled on your side, we use the KMS to decrypt only within the runtime. I'll send the detailed crypto flow — apologies if I mangle terms, sometimes transcriptions say "kay vee cache" and we mean KV cache, but I'll share the doc.
[02:10] Sara: We need to see SOC 2 type II evidence and a security questionnaire. Also retention: we want logs for 90 days, but models should not persist any PII beyond the request.
[02:22] Maya: Understood. We have SOC 2 and ISO docs; I'll attach those and the security questionnaire after the call. For retention, we support configurable retention windows and audit logs; default is 30 days but enterprise can configure 90+ and mask or not persist inputs to model cache.
[02:40] Dr. Alicia: On performance — our SLAs are 200ms p95 for short prompts under 512 tokens. Can you get close to that? Latency is a big deal for the triage UI.
[02:50] Jordan: Short answer: depends on model and infra. With low-latency GPUs and optimized runtime we can hit sub-200ms for very small prompts on dedicated instances; if you need that production SLO we recommend Dedicated reserved capacity or private pinned nodes. We'll validate in the pilot.
[03:10] Marcus: Cost is a concern, too. If we go dedicated, how do we balance cost vs latency?
[03:16] Jordan: There are levers: batching, quantization, and model choice. We typically start with a mid-size open model quantized to 4-bit for cost; if latency is strict, we move to a faster variant or smaller context lengths and pinned GPUs. We'll show the tradeoff matrix in the benchmark plan.
[03:32] Tom: For integration, do you expose a REST API and webhooks? Our platform consumes REST endpoints.
[03:36] Dan: Yes REST + SDKs, streaming supported. Also server-to-server auth with mTLS or token-based keys; in VPC you can also restrict egress and use private endpoints.
[03:46] Sara: About SSO — we have Okta. We need SAML SSO for RBAC to map roles to environment permissions.
[03:54] Maya: We support SAML and OIDC; we'll provide the SSO setup doc. For RBAC we support role mapping and org-level admin controls.
[04:05] Dr. Alicia: Pilot dataset — we will scrub PII and share a small sample (about 10k examples) to validate quality and latency. Is that enough?
[04:14] Jordan: That's perfect for an initial run. We'll need schema and a few representative query patterns. We'll run baseline throughput and p95 latency tests.
[04:24] Marcus: Network — we'll want details on required ports, CIDR ranges, and whether we need to open egress to a Redwood control plane. Our security team prefers minimal egress.
[04:34] Dan: For Private, we can operate with customer-managed control plane connectivity via private link or peering. We'll provide a networking checklist; sometimes we need a small control plane channel for telemetry, but we can accommodate strict egress policies.
[04:50] Sara: Please include audit log format, fields, and retention options in the security pack you send.
[04:56] Maya: Will do.
[05:00] [05:00] Jordan: Quick note on evals: we recommend a small set of evaluation prompts included in the pilot that exercise edge cases for hallucination, privacy, and safety. We'll attach a sample eval harness.
[05:12] Dr. Alicia: Great. About rollout — after pilot, what's typical timeline to go to prod?
[05:18] Maya: If pilot is successful, typical ramp is 4-8 weeks depending on infra approvals and SSO. For enterprise with private deployment we often see longer due to network and security approvals.
[05:30] Marcus: Our compliance window is tight — we'd like production in 8 weeks if possible.
[05:34] Maya: We'll aim for that, and Jordan will indicate blockers in the bench plan.
[05:40] Tom: Any limitations on model debugging or access to logs? We need token-level visibility for debugging requests.
[05:46] Jordan: You get per-request tracing, token counts, latency breakdowns, and we can expose debugging hooks. In Private mode you control log retention. There may be minor sensitive fields redacted by default but can be toggled with controls.
[06:00] [06:00] Dr. Alicia: One last thing — legal/procurement is looped in; we'll likely have a standard enterprise contract with an SLA. Who handles that?
[06:08] Maya: Our commercial team handles contracts; I'll connect you to them. Meanwhile I'll send standard SOW and pricing ranges for Dedicated vs Private so you can prep procurement.
[06:18] Marcus: Sounds good.
[06:20] Jordan: I'll summarize the technical deliverables: benchmarking plan, infra checklist, SSO flow, security questionnaire, network requirements.
[06:28] Dan: And I'll include the Kubernetes/VM sizing guidance for on-prem and guidance on quantization profiles we recommend.
[06:36] Sara: Please also include the options for KMS integration and the exact encryption flow diagram.
[06:41] Jordan: Yep, diagram will be included.
[06:44] [15:00] -- NOTE: conversation jumps, filler --
[15:10] Maya: Quick recap: next steps are send docs, customer to share sample data and network contacts, schedule VPC deep-dive.
[15:22] Dr. Alicia: Confirmed.
[15:26] Marcus: We'll target sending network contacts by 2027-08-25, sample dataset by 2027-08-30.
[15:34] Sara: Security questionnaire by 2027-08-26, noted.
[15:38] Maya: Great. Any other questions?
[15:41] Tom: Nothing else on my side.
[15:43] Dr. Alicia: No, all good.
[15:45] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the playbook and schedule the VPC deep-dive for next week.
[15:51] Jordan: Thanks all.
[15:53] End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "kay-vee cache" for KV cache), speaker overlaps, and some timestamps are approximate.
